grouping_reason: One characteristic-free multivariate divided-derivative operator with coefficient computation, coefficient-change and injective-renaming naturality, iteration, disjoint support, ordinary-partial compatibility, degree/vanishing bounds, independent-factor rule and factorial bridge. These use one coherent parent operator and should not be presented as eleven independent one-lemma PRs against an absent parent.
implementation_and_verdict_distinctions: Keep separately assessed scalar hasseCoeff alias out of the list of independently accepted YES contributions; inline its product or keep an internal implementation helper after upstream design review.

The operator still needs a monomial/computational interface and routine zero/additive laws even when those have separate NO/private verdicts. An independent upstream contribution verdict does not forbid minimal supporting implementation/API in the coherent module.

Prefer the verified sharp coordinate degree bound as primary companion and retain the accepted weak degree-preservation corollary used by callers. Coordinate degree estimates do not by themselves imply zero under natural degree conventions, so retain the separate annihilation interface.
Keep coefficient cocycle/successor and monomial-independent-factor helpers private unless a separate public API case is made.
A full multivariate Hasse Leibniz theorem is a proposed companion gap, not already verified existing mathlib API.

The factorial identity is an interface between characteristic-free Hasse operators and iterated ordinary partial derivations; factorial inversion requires additional coefficient hypotheses and must not be generalized silently in positive characteristic.
layering: Keep the core module algebraic. Downstream Taylor, coefficient-norm estimates, Wronskians, fraction-field/descent and Roth numerical bounds should depend on this parent module rather than becoming imports of it.
